meta.title: Lawn Mowing in Holly, MI | Grand Scapes
meta.description: Weekly lawn mowing in Holly, MI by Grand Scapes: mowed, trimmed, edged and blown off, on sandy hills, lake lots and tight village yards alike.

hero.title: Mowed higher on **sandy ground.**
hero.lede: Grand Scapes mows Holly lawns every week: mowed, trimmed, edged along the walks and drive, and blown off, finished in clean stripes. On the sandy hills and lake lots around Holly, Rob talks mowing height with you before the first cut.

local.title: Three kinds of ground **under Holly lawns.**
local.intro: Much of Holly Township sits on sand and gravel, the village on heavier soil, and the lake and wetland edges on wet muck. Each one mows differently: sandy lawns brown out first in a dry stretch, low spots stay soft after rain, and the hills take careful passes to keep the stripes even.

points.title: Taller grass for dry spells
points.body: MSU Extension recommends mowing Michigan lawns at 3.5 inches, which builds a bigger root system and helps grass ride out drought. On sand, which holds less water than loam, that height keeps more of the lawn green through August.

points.title: Soft ground near the water
points.body: Lawns that run down to a lake or a wetland edge stay soft after a heavy rain. A wet strip gets a lighter pass or waits for the next visit, since ruts in soft turf take a long time to grow out.

points.title: Hills and wooded edges
points.body: Much of Holly Township is hilly, and plenty of lots back up to woods or state land. Slopes get mowed where a mower can work safely, the tree line gets trimmed by hand, and we pick up sticks before we mow.

points.title: Tight village lots
points.body: Village lots are tighter, with walks, curbs and alleys on more than one side. That is trimmer and edger work, and the clippings get blown back onto the grass instead of into the street or the neighbor's drive.

logistics.title: A mowing week in Holly, start to finish.
body: Mowing runs weekly through the growing season. Each visit the grass is cut, the edges along the drive, walks and curbs are trimmed and edged, and every hard surface is blown clean.

Lake lots, gated drives and dogs in the yard go on the notes at the first visit, so the crew knows how to get in and what to close behind them. If you spend part of the summer away, the lawn keeps getting cut without you there.

In fall the mowing keeps going until the grass stops growing, and the late cuts pick up leaves as they go. When the leaves come down faster than a mower can handle, a [fall cleanup](/leaf-removal-holly-mi/) takes over.

faq.q: Do you mow lawns in Holly, MI?
faq.a: Yes. Grand Scapes mows lawns every week in the Village of Holly and out in Holly Township. Each visit includes mowing, trimming, edging along the hard edges and blowing off the drive and walks. Rob comes out first and gives you a free estimate.

faq.q: How high should I mow a lawn on sandy soil?
faq.a: About 3.5 inches, which is what MSU Extension recommends for Michigan lawns, and sandy ground is where that height pays off most. Sand holds less water than loam, so short grass on it browns quickly in July and August. Taller grass grows deeper roots and crowds out weeds.

faq.q: When is the last mow of the year in Michigan?
faq.a: There is no fixed date. Keep mowing until the grass stops growing, which shifts with the weather every fall. MSU turf specialists also say to mulch or remove the leaves before winter, because a leaf mat left on the lawn can smother it and invite snow mold.

faq.q: Do you mow lake lots that slope down to the water?
faq.a: Yes, with care. Steep pitches near a shoreline get mowed where a mower can work safely and trimmed by hand where it cannot. If the bottom of the lawn is still soft from rain, it waits for the next visit rather than getting torn up.
